name: YourEthos
tagline: An AI tool that builds a profile of your values and beliefs, then uses it to guide or personalize advice and decisions.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanics here are not exotic: a structured questionnaire, an LLM call that turns the answers into a values profile, and a chat surface that keeps that profile in the system prompt. An agent can build all of that in a weekend, and the personal version has an honest advantage, your profile stays on your machine instead of in someone else's database. What you cannot one-shot is the part that makes the output feel authoritative: a well-designed instrument, questions that actually discriminate between values rather than flattering you, and prompt scaffolding that has been tuned against real users. You will get something that works and something that occasionally reads like a horoscope. Given how little of this category is verifiable, that gap may matter less than it sounds.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that walks you through a values questionnaire, distills the answers into a persistent profile document, and then answers your questions and decisions through that profile.
requirements: An LLM API key (Anthropic or OpenAI) in .env
Willingness to write or adapt your own question set
whatYouLose: A professionally designed assessment instrument instead of questions you wrote at midnight
Any comparative context, no sense of how your profile sits against anyone else's
Polished report layouts and shareable summaries
Mobile access unless you host it somewhere
Whatever prompt tuning the vendor did to keep outputs from drifting into fortune cookie territory
moatNotes: The defensible asset in values profiling is the instrument and the aggregate response data, not the chat layer on top of it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because designing a questionnaire that produces a profile you actually believe is real work, and most people do not want to spend a weekend arguing with themselves about whether question seven is leading. There is also a credibility effect: a profile handed to you by a product feels like a finding, while a profile generated by a script you wrote yesterday feels like something you made up. That is not entirely irrational, the vendor has seen thousands of response patterns and you have seen one.
notes: The chat layer is trivial; the questionnaire is the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first "values profile" web app in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for storage, single file at ./data/ethos.db.
- One LLM provider: Anthropic via the official SDK. Key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local. Commit a .env.example, never a real key.
- No auth, no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry. Single user on localhost.

What it does:
1. Onboarding: a multi-step questionnaire, one question per screen, progress bar, answers saved to SQLite as you go so a refresh does not lose work. Seed it with 24 questions in a JSON file at ./content/questions.json. Mix formats: forced-choice tradeoffs between two competing values, 1-7 agreement scales, and three free-text prompts about a real decision the user regretted. Make the file trivially editable so questions can be replaced.
2. Synthesis: a server action that sends all answers to the model and returns structured JSON: 6-10 named values with a short definition in the user's own framing, ranked; 3 tensions between values that will predictably cause friction; 3 blind spots. Store the result as a versioned profile row with a timestamp. Never overwrite, always append a new version.
3. Profile page: renders the current profile, shows version history, lets the user edit any value description by hand and save it as a new version. Hand edits are authoritative and must be marked as such.
4. Consult: a chat page. Every request injects the current profile into the system prompt and instructs the model to reason from those stated values, to name which value is in play, and to flag when two values conflict rather than picking one silently. Persist conversations in SQLite.
5. Export: a button that dumps everything, answers, all profile versions, all chats, to a single JSON file, plus a Markdown rendering of the current profile.

Explicitly out of scope: sharing, multi-user, comparison against population norms, any hosted deployment, payment, email, mobile app, PDF generation.

Honesty requirement: put a persistent one-line disclaimer in the footer noting this is a self-authored instrument with no validation behind it.

Deliver a README with setup in under six commands and a note on where to edit questions.json.
